entries.principle: Safety, proportionality, and prevention of harm
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), principles of proportionality/do no harm and safety/security
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V, On Personal Data and Their Protection (2013)
entries.why_here: Input validation rejects impossible values before model processing, preventing invalid data from producing unreliable scholarship decisions and limiting processing to relevant, legitimate purposes.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), fairness and non-discrimination principle
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan
entries.why_here: Baseline matched-pair testing showed outcome flips and score differences for name and university attributes, so these irrelevant fields are hidden to reduce proxy discrimination.

entries.principle: Proportionality, do no harm, privacy, and legitimate purpose
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), proportionality/do no harm and privacy principles
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V, On Personal Data and Their Protection (2013)
entries.why_here: The harness refuses prohibited purposes, minors, missing consent, and invalid inputs instead of processing requests that are unsafe, unauthorized, or outside the legitimate scholarship-screening purpose.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 42-43
entries.instrument: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021)
entries.why_here: The structured decision log records the decision, controls, reason code, model and prompt versions, fields shown or withheld, and timestamp to support auditing and accountability.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 35-36
entries.instrument: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021)
entries.why_here: Borderline or conflicting decisions are escalated to a human reviewer because the scholarship outcome can affect applicants and ultimate responsibility must remain with people.
